topic: Deposition Procedures & Witness Preparation
supporting_evidence: The witness confirmed she had not previously been deposed, acknowledged the penalty of perjury, and confirmed that no health issues would prevent her from providing her best testimony.

anchors.start_quote: At the beginning of a deposition, I always make sure that somebody knows kind of how the process works, and one of my first questions to do that is to ask you if you've ever had your deposition taken before.
anchors.end_quote: Terrific.  Thank you very much.

topic: Expert Retention & Scope of Testimony

anchors.start_quote: So you had been retained as an expert in that -- in this case; correct?

topic: Identification of Expert Report

topic: SBPB Policy Agenda and Core Advocacy Areas
supporting_evidence: The witness described SBPB's policy agenda as focusing on three main areas: ensuring adequate protections in the federal student loan safety net, addressing racial equity and discrimination in the lending marketplace, and combating predatory student lending practices by schools.

anchors.start_quote: Bullet Point 1 sort of says a little bit about your duties there, and it mentions that you're trying to execute SBPB's policy agenda.
anchors.end_quote: And particularly in the private student loan market, we also look -- examine the practices of schools across the country and how they result in -- how their practices result in their students and their students' families going into debt.

topic: Student Loan Debt Cancellation Campaign
supporting_evidence: The witness clarified that the 'canceling student loan debt' reference pertains to a national campaign addressing the burden of federal student loans in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic and President Biden's proposal to cancel up to $20,000 in debt, noting that the President subsequently made that policy decision.

anchors.start_quote: The second bullet point states that it is a national leader in the campaign to cancel student loan debt.

They clarified that while they have not worked as a loan servicer or studied servicing in formal education, they gained expertise through legal aid work starting in 2009 and research at the National Consumer Law Center.

topic: Student Loan Servicer Oversight & Contract Review
supporting_evidence: The witness described providing comments to the Department of Education regarding student loan servicing contracts and Requests for Information (RFIs). These comments focused on ensuring consumer protections, adequate oversight of servicer conduct, and practical operational issues such as language access and call center staffing, with testimony before Congress also conducted in this capacity.

anchors.start_quote: And have you worked on any initiatives that were directed at student loan servicers?
anchors.end_quote: Those were both done in my capacity at the National Consumer Law Center.

topic: Loan Portfolio Transfers
supporting_evidence: The witness confirmed that loan portfolio transfers between servicers are a frequent occurrence in the federal student loan context, estimating it has happened approximately a dozen times, including recent departures by servicers such as Navient.

anchors.start_quote: Ms. Yu, in -- in any of your work experience, have you ever dealt with a situation where one loan servicer takes over a student loan portfolio from another loan servicer?

topic: Student Loan Servicing Transfers and Associated Risks
supporting_evidence: The witness described the transfer of federal and private student loan portfolios between servicers, noting that while transfers are common, they carry risks such as data loss, lost payments, and borrower confusion. The witness confirmed that in their experience, a follow-on servicer always steps in when one exits the market.

anchors.start_quote: Most -- so most recently we saw, for example, Navient left the Department of Education's loan portfolio, and the loans were transferred to the company Maximus, which runs a servicer called Aidvantage.
anchors.end_quote: I am not aware of any instance where that has occurred.

topic: Regulatory Compliance for Data Transfers in This Case
supporting_evidence: The witness identified state laws, such as the California State Student Loan Servicing Law, that regulate data transfers. However, the witness stated they could not opine on whether regulations were violated during the specific 2011 transfer of PEAKS loans from Access Group to Vervent (First Associates) due to scope limitations and lack of access to relevant documents.

anchors.start_quote: Are you -- are you aware of any regulations that apply to the manner in which student loan servicing data is supposed to be transferred from the original servicer to the follow-on servicer when there's a change in student loan servicing?
anchors.end_quote: That's outside the scope of what I was asked to look at in this case, and I don't have -- I don't have access to the documents of what was transferred and couldn't make an opinion about what rules were or were not violated.

topic: Witness Expertise and Analysis of ITT Student Debt
supporting_evidence: The witness confirmed familiarity with for-profit colleges and clarified that their expertise lies in student lending rather than educational quality. They testified to having represented individual ITT borrowers and analyzed systemic issues regarding student debt incurred at ITT, citing findings from regulators and Senate committees.

anchors.start_quote: You provide -- the initial background, you provide an overview of higher education and for-profit colleges.
anchors.end_quote: So I did -- I -- I have both on individual level -- I -- I represented individual borrowers and -- who have a -- I've represented a small number of ITT students; however, my expertise has been looking more broadly at ITT and about the systemic problems that have been identified by regulators, by, also, Senate committees, and so looked systemically at the issues that have been raised by student loan borrowers in those contexts and understanding the ways in which ITT has led students into debt.

topic: Economic Outcomes and Value of ITT Education
supporting_evidence: The witness stated that very few ITT students receive the promised benefits, leading to debt burdens that outweigh the educational value. They noted that ITT graduates typically earn less than high school graduates and highlighted high dropout rates, referencing a 2012 Senate HELP Committee report on retention rates.

anchors.start_quote: Would it be fair to say that your view about ITT, based on the -- the materials you've reviewed, is that in many occasions the benefits of an ITT education were outweighed by the burdens of debt that students took?
anchors.end_quote: I believe -- the Senate HELP Committee looked specifically at ITT and looked at the retention rates at ITT.

topic: ITT Student Outcomes and Institutional Quality Metrics
supporting_evidence: The witness testified that ITT had notably high default rates and that individual student success stories are outliers rather than indicative of the institution's overall quality, emphasizing the importance of aggregate data such as retention and default rates.

anchors.end_quote: So yes, there are -- there are going to be example of students who make decent salaries, but that is not necessarily an indication. You have to look instead rather at the bigger picture of what's -- what's happening across the field.

topic: Consequences of Failure to Provide Final Disclosures
supporting_evidence: The witness testified that if final disclosures are not provided, the loan is invalid and unenforceable, granting the borrower an indefinite right to cancel until the disclosures are received. The witness explained that cancellation results in the return of funds to the lender and the extinguishment of borrower obligations, and noted that other factors, such as misleading practices or lack of informed consent under the Truth in Lending Act, can also impact loan enforceability.

anchors.start_quote: The final disclosures.  What is your opinion as to whether or not the final disclosures were sent to the PEAKS borrowers?
anchors.end_quote: That is to make sure that, you know, that students have an under- -- or borrowers, consumers have an understanding of the total cost of credit.

supporting_evidence: The witness testified that CFPB and Department of Education findings, though temporally post-origination, related to origination events and that the subsequent cancellation of loans within the CFPB settlement rendered them unenforceable. The witness clarified that the CFPB settlement did not specifically find the Vervent defendants at fault regarding the PEAKS loans.
